subject: Azure Marketplace private listing — vendor evidence & co-sell commercial questions
messages:
From: Sara Powell <sara.powell@cloudwave.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: azurepm@microsoft.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure Marketplace private listing — initial evidence & co-sell questions

Hi Markus / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really excited to get CloudWave listed as a private offer in the Azure Marketplace with Redwood as the co-sell partner. Per our discussion, attaching the initial compliance and technical artifacts you asked for:

- CloudWave_SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (redacted)
- network-diagram-cloudwave-v2.pdf
- data-isolation-attestation.docx

Quick clarifications from our side:
1) Azure asked whether Redwood will require customer-level separate VNet peering for every private offer or whether a shared managed gateway is acceptable. Our security team prefers managed gateway but can adopt per-customer isolation if required.
2) For co-sell registration, we need a revenue share template and any templated language Redwood prefers in the listing (e.g., subscription vs. usage billing callouts).
3) Procurement: can you confirm Redwood's preferred PO flow for marketplace purchases and whether Redwood supports net-45 payment terms for enterprise purchases?

Next steps we want to keep moving: evidence review and a short legal sync to align on minimal contract addenda for the marketplace private SKU. We can do a quick call next week 4/22–4/23.

Attaching artifacts as requested; let us know if you need unsanitized SOC sections under an NDA.

Best,
Sara Powell
Head of Partnerships, CloudWave Inc.
[sara.powell@cloudwave.com]

Subject: Re: Azure Marketplace private listing — initial evidence & co-sell questions

Sara — thanks for sending these through and for the quick turnaround. A few points from our side after an initial pass:

1) Evidence review: SOC2 doc and network diagram look reasonable at a glance. Marissa (legal) will do the deeper review for any redactions/PII. If your SOC has a bridge letter or an auditor contact, please include it.

2) Network isolation: Redwood's private offering supports both patterns. For initial go‑to‑market we generally recommend the managed gateway pattern for faster onboarding, with an opt-in per-customer VNet peering path for regulated customers. Action: please confirm whether CloudWave can support optional per-customer VNet peering within 6 weeks if a customer requests it.

3) Commercials / co-sell: Ben — can you share Redwood's current co-sell revenue share template? Our typical starting split for private marketplace offers is 15% referral fee to ISV partner (CloudWave) / 85% to platform billing, but we have flexibility for enterprise anchor deals. Sara — can you share CloudWave's target split and whether you plan to invoice via Azure Marketplace or direct invoicing?

4) Procurement & PO flow: We support PO/net-45 on a case-by-case basis for Annual Reserved commitments. Standard marketplace purchases are billed via Azure Marketplace and settle through the Marketplace billing flow (we can accept invoice-routing for custom SOWs). If you need net-45 for marketplace subscription purchases, we'll need sign-off from finance.

Proposed next steps:
- Marissa to request any missing SOC details / confirm NDA for deeper docs (by 4/23).
- CloudWave to confirm VNet peering capability and preferred commercial split (by 4/23).
- Quick sync Thurs 4/22 11am PT to align commercial/technical owners (Markus, Ben, Sara).

Thanks — I'll book the call pending confirmation.

— Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Markus / Ben — following up after our internal security team review. Short answers below and attached a slightly expanded network diagram showing the managed gateway flow and the optional peering overlay.

- VNet peering capability: Yes — CloudWave can enable per-customer VNet peering within ~4 weeks from technical kickoff (we confirmed resource templates exist). We can also support managed gateway as a default for pilot customers.
- Commercial split: CloudWave's commercial target is a 70/30 split (Redwood/CloudWave) for co-sell registration credits; however, CloudWave is flexible to negotiate on a per-deal basis for larger enterprise anchors.
- Billing model: CloudWave prefers to have marketplace subscription billing (Azure Marketplace-managed) for ease of procurement for customers. Invoice-routing for bespoke SOWs is acceptable.
- PO terms: Procurement asked if Redwood can accept net-30 for marketplace-backed annual commitments. Procurement team cc'd on this thread (procurement@cloudwave.com).

Attachments: network-diagram-cloudwave-v2-annotated.pdf

We can do the 4/22 11am PT call as proposed — I think the agenda should be: 1) confirm technical onboarding pattern; 2) co-sell revenue split expectations; 3) procurement/payment path; 4) timing for finalizing marketplace listing and legal addenda.

Thanks,
Sara

Sara / team — thanks for the artifacts and the follow-up. I did a legal/compliance pass and have the following notes and requests to keep the marketplace onboarding smooth:

1) SOC2 access: We appreciate the redacted SOC2. To complete the security review we need either (a) an auditor attestation or (b) a secure link to a non-redacted SOC2 under an NDA. If you prefer an NDA, Redwood will sign a standard mutual NDA (I can circulate).

2) Data residency / isolation: Please confirm in writing that customer data is logically segregated per tenant and that CloudWave retains no rights to customer data beyond what's necessary for service delivery. The data-isolation-attestation.docx is a good start — please sign/return on company letterhead.

3) Contracting / addendum: For Azure private offers we typically require a short addendum to the master subscription terms covering: indemnity carve-outs for marketplace billing, support SLAs, and data processing terms (DPA). I've attached a one‑page addendum template as a baseline (ATT: redwood-marketplace-addendum-v1.docx). Please review and propose any redlines.

4) Commercials: Redwood uses HubSpot deal records to track co-sell revenue splits. Ben, please confirm the mechanical steps for registering co-sell and whether Redwood will publish the listing with CloudWave's target 70/30 split or keep the listing neutral while capturing the split in our CRM (we usually capture split in CRM and surface it to Azure PM for co-sell credits).

5) Procurement terms: Net-30 on a marketplace subscription is not standard since Azure settles through its marketplace flow; however, for annual committed contracts that are invoiced directly we can accept net-30 after finance approval. Please flag which customers will require invoiced annual commitments vs marketplace-managed subscriptions.

If we can get: signed data-attestation, SOC2 auditor contact or NDA, and confirmation on billing preference by 5/3, legal can finalize the addendum and Emily in Ops can schedule the Azure private SKU creation the week of 5/10.

Proposed meeting: Thurs 4/29 11am PT to run through the addendum and the transition plan. Markus — can you confirm?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
